pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8 (GPIO0)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. No onboard user button on this board (checked against the vendor schematic - see notes.txt) - only a non-GPIO RESET button (SW1) is present

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D9
pins.label: D9 (GPIO2)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. No onboard LED confirmed on this GPIO - the pins_arduino.h LED_BUILTIN=2 alias has no corresponding hardware LED on this board (checked against the vendor schematic - see notes.txt); this board's status/overcurrent LEDs are driven by the TPS2041BD/TPS2051BD power-switch ICs and the PIC16F1455 USB-serial bridge, not by the ESP8266

pins.name: D0
pins.label: D0 (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D10
pins.label: D10 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D2
pins.label: D2 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. This board has an on-board resistor-divider (R15=220K series, R16=100K to GND, per the vendor schematic) giving A0 a 0-3.2V range instead of the bare chip's native 0-1.0V - see adc note below
